AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: We observed a particular resistance phenotype: an E. coli isolate from urine sample exhibited resistance to mecillinam (Amd) but was fully susceptible to other β-lactam antibiotics (Amd-R-BL-S). Our objectives were to determine the prevalence of this phenotype and to describe their phenotype, molecular epidemiology and genetic background.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Between the 1st Jan 2014 and the 31st Jan 2016, Amd-R-BL-S E. coli isolates from urine were collected. We analysed genes previously reported as mostly involved in Amd resistance. We investigated the genetic relatedness by rep-PCR completed by MLST.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Ten Amd-R-BL-S isolates were collected, accounted for 0.39% of all E. coli obtained from urine samples (10/2547), 0.88% of ampicillin-susceptible E. coli urine (10/1135) and 9.6% of Amd-R E. coli (10/104). The isolates appeared as small colonies, had round morphology and an impaired fitness. The isolates were not clonal and belonged to various extra-intestinal or commensal E. coli phylogroups. Mutations in cysb were evidenced for all clinical isolates.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Microbiologists should be aware of these isolates with a particular susceptibility phenotype, which is not due to error in disk diffusion but is a real non-enzymatic antibiotic resistance pattern.
